Data entry, transcription, or calibration error: systematic sign inversion, scaling miscalibration, or systematic offset in one or more streams during baseline setup or ongoing data logging
Shared environmental driver (temperature, pressure, electromagnetic field) with instruments exhibiting opposite-sign or phase-delayed mechanical responses
Instrumental coupling (mechanical vibration, electromagnetic interference, or resonant mode coupling) between instruments sharing lab space, with opposite-sign response or damping feedback
Spurious cross-correlations arising from multiple-comparison bias and weak within-instrument autocorrelation, inflated by scanning many time offsets and instrument pairs

Systematic calibration error or sign inversion in one or more instruments during baseline setup (days 1–10), propagating through all downstream readings and cross-correlations.

Shared environmental driver (temperature, barometric pressure, or electromagnetic field fluctuation) with differential time-response or phase-lag across instruments due to distinct mounting orientations, thermal mass, or electromagnetic coupling symmetries established during baseline.

Weak instrumental cross-talk or anti-phase coupling in lab space (pendulum_lab and resonator_lab share mounting platform or power distribution), with characteristic response time of several days due to low-Q damping or nonlinear feedback.
Multiple-comparison bias and weak autocorrelation inflated by scanning many time offsets and instrument pairs, creating spurious negative sign bias in a subset of correlations.
No real anomaly; all patterns are consistent with independent random measurement error, and the negative sign bias is a chance fluctuation.
Genuine physical drift in pendulum_lab during days 11–25: thermal equilibration, mechanical settling, or persistent environmental effect specific to pendulum_lab mounting or environment.

Baseline calibration error in pendulum_lab (systematic offset or timing misalignment during days 1–10) creates apparent drift when post-baseline readings revert to true instrumental output, inflating the z-score.

The negative cross-correlations observed in the previous analysis (e.g., pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_lab: r=−0.142) are real and reflect systematic environmental or instrumental coupling, but today's data do not yet contain enough power to falsify or confirm this pattern. The pendulum_lab drift may be a separate phenomenon, unrelated to cross-instrument correlations.

Random noise and multiple-comparison bias; all observed patterns (drift, correlations, lags) are consistent with independent measurement error, and perceived anomalies reflect p-hacking or cherry-picked offset scanning.

Something unconsidered: a hidden temporal structure, non-stationarity, or data-collection artifact in pendulum_lab specifically (e.g., operator bias, sensor age-out, or trial-numbering errors creating spurious ordering effects).

Pendulum_lab baseline (days 1–10) was systematically offset low by ~0.0007 beats due to calibration error, timing misalignment, or environmental transient; post-baseline readings reflect true instrument output and appear to drift only because the baseline is wrong. The negative cross-correlations with other instruments may reflect sign inversion or systematic bias propagating through cross-validation.

Genuine physical drift in pendulum_lab during days 11–25 (thermal equilibration, mechanical settling, or persistent environmental effect specific to pendulum_lab mounting, location, or operator); instrument reached stable new equilibrium by day 25 and has remained there through day 35. Other instruments unaffected due to independent physical drivers or superior environmental stability.

The negative cross-correlations observed in earlier analysis (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_lab r=−0.172 at 6-day lag; pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_lab r=−0.268 at 6-day lag) reflect real systematic instrumental or environmental coupling with multi-day lag, unrelated to pendulum_lab drift. Coupling may involve shared environmental driver (humidity, vibration, temperature gradient) or instrumental cross-talk (e.g., pendulum vibration damping resonator response with delay). The pendulum_lab drift is a separate phenomenon.

All observed patterns (pendulum_lab drift, negative cross-correlations, apparent lags) are consistent with random noise, measurement error, and multiple-comparison bias from scanning offsets across 1–12 day lags. Perceived anomalies reflect cherry-picked offset windows and p-hacking.

Hidden temporal structure, data-collection artifact, or procedural error specific to pendulum_lab (e.g., operator bias, sensor age-out, trial-numbering error, or environmental factor unique to pendulum_lab location). Baseline calibration may be correct, but post-baseline procedure diverged from baseline protocol.

Pendulum_lab baseline (days 1–10) was systematically offset low by ~0.0007 beats due to calibration error, timing misalignment, environmental transient, or incomplete mechanical settling. Post-baseline readings reflect true stable instrument output. The appearance of 'drift' is an artifact of baseline miscalibration.

Genuine physical drift in pendulum_lab during days 11–25 (thermal equilibration, mechanical creep, or environmental settling specific to pendulum apparatus); instrument reached stable new equilibrium by ~day 25 and has remained there through day 36. Other instruments unaffected due to independent environmental drivers or superior environmental stability.

Procedural or data-collection error specific to pendulum_lab post-baseline workflow (operator bias, sensor degradation, trial-numbering artifact, or environmental factor unique to pendulum_lab location). Baseline calibration may be correct, but post-baseline procedure diverged from baseline protocol, or data were mis-recorded.

Random noise and multiple-comparison artifact: observed patterns reflect measurement error and cherry-picked offset windows across 1–12 day lags. No true anomaly exists; all instruments output independent Gaussian noise around constant means.

Pendulum_lab baseline (days 1–10) was systematically offset low due to calibration, timing, or environmental transient; post-baseline readings reflect true stable output. The asymmetry between pendulum_lab and pendulum_obs is explained by instrument-specific baseline error, not physics.

Genuine physical drift in pendulum_lab apparatus (thermal settling of pivot, damping fluid transient, mechanical creep in mount) occurred days 11–25 and reached stable equilibrium by day 25. Pendulum_obs is insensitive to this drift due to different measurement principle or environmental decoupling.

Procedural or data-handling error specific to pendulum_lab post-baseline workflow: operator protocol shift, sensor degradation, trial-numbering artifact, or environmental factor unique to pendulum_lab location that began on day 11 and remained constant through day 40.

Random noise, measurement error, and multiple-comparison artifact: observed patterns are statistical noise emerging from scanning 1–12 day offset windows. No true anomaly exists; all instruments output constant means with independent Gaussian noise.
Residual: an explanatory pattern not yet considered.
